Read Bank of Japan observations for exact series codes

Source: R/api.R
read_boj_series.Rd

Fetches observations from the official Bank of Japan (BOJ) Time-Series Data Search getDataCode route for one or more exact series codes. Input codes are sent in batches of at most 250 (the API limit), and every NEXTPOSITION cursor returned by the service is followed in order. JSON null values and CSV blank values remain rows rather than being dropped. Use read_boj_snapshot() to parse a saved response without a network request, or boj_provenance() to inspect the identity of responses used by this function.

Usage

read_boj_series(
  db,
  code,
  start_date = NULL,
  end_date = NULL,
  language = "en",
  format = "json",
  cache_dir = boj_cache_dir(),
  refresh = FALSE,
  offline = FALSE,
  max_age = 24 * 60 * 60,
  timeout = 30,
  retries = 3L,
  wait = 1,
  max_bytes = 128 * 1024^2,
  max_pages = 100L,
  max_cells = 1000000L,
  max_codes_total = 5000L,
  deadline = NULL
)

Arguments

db

A BOJ database identifier, such as "FM08". It is converted to uppercase after validation; an identifier with a syntactically valid shape can still be rejected by the BOJ API if that database is not available.

code

A non-empty character vector of exact series codes without the database prefix. Values must be non-missing, non-empty and unique. The vector is limited by max_codes_total and split into API batches of 250.

start_date

Optional inclusive lower period bound as one YYYY or YYYYPP code. NULL omits the bound from the request.

end_date

Optional inclusive upper period bound as one YYYY or YYYYPP code. NULL omits the bound; when both bounds are supplied, start_date must not be later than end_date.

language

Response language: exactly "en" or "jp". The value controls the language fields returned by BOJ and, for CSV responses, the transfer encoding.

format

Official response format, "json" or "csv"; matching is case-insensitive. JSON responses are parsed as UTF-8, while Japanese CSV responses are decoded as CP932.

cache_dir

Character path to the snapshot cache. The default is boj_cache_dir(), which uses the readboj.cache_dir option or tools::R_user_dir("readboj", "cache"). Missing cache subdirectories are created as needed.

refresh

Logical flag. When TRUE, bypasses a current cached request snapshot and obtains a fresh response. It is validated even when offline = TRUE.

offline

Logical flag. When TRUE, requires a valid cached snapshot and makes no network request. It is useful for deterministic replay.

max_age

Non-negative number of seconds for which a cached snapshot is considered current; Inf permits any age. The default is 24 hours.

timeout

Non-negative number of seconds allowed for each HTTP attempt. The default is 30 seconds; the call-wide deadline remains authoritative.

retries

Non-negative whole number of retries for transient transport or HTTP failures. The default is 3; non-transient failures are not retried.

wait

Non-negative number of seconds used between pages, code batches and retries. It is skipped for offline reads and is bounded by deadline.

max_bytes

Positive maximum decompressed response bytes per page. The default is 128 MiB; oversized responses fail with readboj_size_error before parsing or caching.

max_pages

Positive whole-number maximum pages allowed for each code batch. The default is 100.

max_cells

Positive whole-number maximum observation rows retained across all batches and pages. The default is 1,000,000.

max_codes_total

Positive whole-number maximum number of input series codes. The default is 5,000; the official per-request 250-code batch limit is applied separately.

deadline

An optional absolute one-element POSIXct or POSIXlt deadline shared by every batch, page, retry and delay. If NULL, a bounded deadline is derived from timeout and retries (at least five minutes). An expired deadline raises readboj_timeout_error.

Value

An ungrouped base data.frame (stringsAsFactors = FALSE) with row names reset and one row per returned observation. The columns are in this exact order and have these types: db, series_code, name_en, name_jp, unit_en, unit_jp, frequency, category_en, and category_jp are character; last_update is Date; period is the exact BOJ period code as character; date is Date; value is numeric; raw_value is the source value as character; and value_status is character. date is the first calendar date inferred from frequency and period, and can be NA when the source code cannot be mapped. JSON missing values have value = NA, raw_value = NA, and value_status = "null"; CSV blank values have value = NA, the original empty raw_value, and value_status = "blank". The returned object has a readboj_provenance attribute; boj_provenance() returns its list of source URL(s), retrieval/cache identity, hashes, response metadata, query, page list, parser schema and package version.

Details

Requests use HTTPS and are restricted to the official BOJ hosts. Successful response bodies are retained as content-addressed snapshots below cache_dir; a valid snapshot is reused while it is within max_age, unless refresh = TRUE. With offline = TRUE, no network request is attempted and the call fails with class readboj_offline_error when a matching valid snapshot is unavailable. Temporary response files are removed after a successful cache write or an error.

Each code batch is paginated independently. The result is never silently deduplicated: duplicate db/series_code/period identities cause a readboj_identity_error. The page, cell, byte, retry and absolute deadline bounds are enforced before unbounded work can occur. The API's latest revised history is returned; this function does not provide vintage or as-of retrieval.

Errors and side effects

Invalid arguments, malformed responses, schema changes, pagination loops, duplicate identities and size limits raise typed readboj_*_error conditions. API and HTTP failures retain response identity in the error where available. The function may perform network I/O and create or update files below cache_dir; it does not write to the current working directory or a global workspace. The default managed cache is in the user-specific location returned by tools::R_user_dir().

Examples

# The packaged response is a small synthetic fixture and is read offline.
json_path <- system.file("extdata", "api-data-page-1.json", package = "readboj")
local_data <- read_boj_snapshot(json_path, type = "data_json", db = "FM08")
local_data[c("series_code", "period", "value", "value_status")]
#>   series_code period  value value_status
#> 1    SYNTHM01 202601 101.25     observed
#> 2    SYNTHM01 202602     NA         null
#> 3    SYNTHM01 202603 103.75     observed

if (identical(Sys.getenv("READBOJ_LIVE_EXAMPLES"), "true")) {
  read_boj_series(
    db = "FM08", code = "FXERM07",
    start_date = "202601", end_date = "202606",
    cache_dir = file.path(tempdir(), "readboj-live-example-cache"),
    timeout = 10, retries = 0L, wait = 0, max_bytes = 8 * 1024^2,
    max_pages = 2L, max_cells = 1000L, max_codes_total = 1L
  )
} else {
  message("Set READBOJ_LIVE_EXAMPLES=true to run the live BOJ example.")
}
#> Set READBOJ_LIVE_EXAMPLES=true to run the live BOJ example.
